## AMENDMENTS TO THE CLAIMS

This listing of claims replaces all prior versions and listings of claims in the application.

**Listing of Claims:**

1. (Currently Amended) A wearable signaling device comprising:
   a flexible band;
   a light emitter mounted on the band;
   a motion sensor configured to detect a hand gesture; and
   a controller that activates the light emitter in response to the hand gesture<u>, wherein the controller selects a blink pattern based on a direction of the hand gesture</u>.

2. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, wherein the light emitter is an LED array.

3. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, further comprising a battery housed in the band.

4. (Currently Amended) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, wherein [[the]] <u>a</u> housing encloses the controller.

5. (Currently Amended) The wearable signaling device of claim 4, wherein the housing is ~~substantially~~ rigid.

6. (Canceled)

7. (Currently Amended) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, wherein the controller reads [[the ]]the sensor at a sampling rate of at least 50 Hz.

8. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, further comprising a dampening member between the band and the light emitter.

9. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, further comprising a signal processing module configured to classify the motion.

10. (Original) A method of signaling a turn, comprising:
   detecting a hand gesture with a motion sensor worn on a wrist; and
   activating a light emitter on a flexible band in response to the hand gesture.

11. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, further comprising a haptic motor that vibrates to confirm the hand gesture.

12. (Original) The method of claim 10, further comprising transmitting a signal to a helmet.

13. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 9, wherein the signal processing module distinguishes a left-turn gesture from a right-turn gesture.

14. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 13, wherein the light emitter displays an amber arrow.

15. (Original) The wearable signaling device of claim 14, wherein the amber arrow points in the direction of the turn.

16. (Withdrawn) A charging dock for the wearable signaling device of claim 1.

17. (Withdrawn) The charging dock of claim 16, comprising an inductive coil.

18. (Withdrawn) The charging dock of claim 17, comprising a status light.

19. (Original) The method of claim 10, wherein the hand gesture is a raised arm.

20. (Original) The method of claim 10, wherein the light emitter flashes at a rate of 2 Hz.

21. (New) The wearable signaling device of claim 1, wherein the flexible band is an elastic strap.

## REMARKS

### Status of the Claims

Claims 1-5 and 7-21 are pending. Claims 1, 4, 5 and 7 are amended, claim 6 is canceled without prejudice or disclaimer, claims 16-18 are withdrawn, and claim 21 is new. Support appears at least at the Detailed Description, paragraphs 1-2, of the application as filed. No new matter is added.

### Objection to the Drawings

A Replacement Sheet for FIG. 2 showing the dampening member 40 of claim 8 is submitted herewith.

### Claim Objections

Claim 7 is amended to delete the repeated word "the" as the Examiner suggested.

### Rejection of Claims 1 and 10 on the Ground of Nonstatutory Double Patenting

Applicant will consider filing a terminal disclaimer when the claims are otherwise allowable.

### Rejection of Claims 4 and 5 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b)

Claim 4 now recites "a housing," which supplies antecedent basis. Claim 5 no longer recites "substantially."

### Rejection of Claims 1-3, 6 and 10 under 35 U.S.C. § 102

Claim 1 now recites that the controller selects a blink pattern based on a direction of the hand gesture. Smith activates its lights with a single fixed pattern (col. 7, ll. 2-15) and does not disclose that limitation. Claims 2 and 3 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons. Claim 6 is canceled, so its rejection is moot. Claim 10 recites detecting a hand gesture with a motion sensor worn on a wrist; Smith's sensor is in a vest.

### Rejection of Claims 4, 5, 7-9, 11, 12, 19 and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103

Jones does not cure the deficiency of Smith with respect to claim 1. Claims 4, 5, 7-9 and 11 depend from claim 1. Claims 12, 19 and 20 depend from claim 10 and are allowable for the reasons given for claim 10.

### Rejection of Claim 11 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Smith, Jones and Park

Park does not cure the deficiency of Smith and Jones with respect to claim 1, from which claim 11 depends.

### Allowable Subject Matter

Applicant thanks the Examiner for indicating that claims 13-15 contain allowable subject matter. Claims 13-15 depend from claim 1 as amended, which Applicant submits is allowable.

### Conclusion

Applicant submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance.
